slices.label: Men outside the South
slices.source: 1890 and 1900 censuses interpolated to November 1892 (1890 from the published state tables; most 1890 schedules were later lost); men 21+ outside the eleven Southern states (including declarant aliens where they could vote); turnout and choice from the backbone, calibrated to certified 1892 returns.

slices.label: Women outside the South
slices.source: 1890 and 1900 censuses interpolated to November 1892 (1890 from the published state tables; most 1890 schedules were later lost); women 21+ outside the South; only Wyoming (a state since 1890) let women vote for president in 1892, so only Wyoming women cast a presidential vote.

slices.label: White Southerners
slices.source: 1890 and 1900 censuses interpolated to November 1892 (1890 from the published state tables; most 1890 schedules were later lost); white adults in the eleven former Confederate states (includes a small number of American Indian and Asian adults); calibrated to certified 1892 returns.

slices.label: Black Southerners
slices.source: 1890 and 1900 censuses interpolated to November 1892 (1890 from the published state tables; most 1890 schedules were later lost); Black adults in the eleven former Confederate states; legal disfranchisement had begun (Mississippi's 1890 constitution, poll taxes in Florida, Tennessee and Arkansas) on top of violence and fraud; the shortfall against white turnout is counted as exclusion.

slices.label: Immigrants not yet citizens
slices.source: 1890 and 1900 censuses interpolated to November 1892 (1890 from the published state tables; most 1890 schedules were later lost); foreign-born white adults who were aliens or had only declared their intent (first papers); declarant aliens could vote in several Midwestern and Western states (fewer each decade as states repealed it), so part of this slice could vote.
